newsitem.title: USA: CBOT says no forced liquidation in July soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT says no forced liquidation in July soybeans.

text.p: Tight U.S. soybean stocks and the resulting volatile trade in CBOT July soybeans has stirred talk of "liquidation only" trade, but officials with the exchange said no such order has been made.
"There is not a liquidation order from the CBOT," said an exchange spokesman.
Under a liquidation order, position holders are only allowed to exit their position as a contract nears expiration.
Speculation about liquidation only trade has been sparked by 20-year lows in U.S. soybean stocks and tight deliverable stocks, floor traders said.
"It's so tight in the old crop that people are wondering whether the CBOT will have liquidation only trade in July," said one floor trader.
As of 1330 CDT Thursday, the amount of soybeans available to deliver against the CBOT July contract was a miniscule 10,000 bushels.

CBOT officials would not say if additional steps were being taken to ensure orderly liquidation of positions in the July contract or if a liquidation order would be considered as expiration draws closer.

"The Chicago Board of Trade always maintains very vigilant monitoring and surveilance of expiration of contracts," CBOT chairman Patrick Arbor said "The expiration of the July soybean contract will be no different than anything we've done before."
July soybeans enter into the period where deliveries can be made against the contract on June 30, and the contract expires on July 22.
The last time the CBOT imposed liquidation only trade was in 1989 during the "Ferruzzi situation," a CBOT spokesman said.
Ferruzzi Finanziaria resigned its membership at the CBOT in 1992 and paid a $2 million fine to settle a dispute over the liquidation of a huge position the company held in soybeans.
